title: Degree-zero cohomology of the constant coefficients on a connected scheme
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $Y$ be a nonempty connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] separated finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k$-scheme, and use the cohomology groups $H^0(Y,\Lambda)=H^0(Y,\Lambda_Y)$ of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] for $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E\}$, with $(A_{E,n})_Y$ the constant sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].

1. For every $n\geq1$, let $1_n\in H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ be the unit class and let $u_n:A_{E,n}\to H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ be the constant-section map induced by the resolution augmentation and exact point sections; $u_n$ is bijective and $u_n(1)=1_n$.

2. Define the coefficient-reduction maps $Q_n:H^0(Y,A_{E,n+1})\to H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ and the projection-induced maps $P_n:H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ from the specified `sfDirectImageTransition`, `SfIntegralDirectImage.projection`, the finite-reduction comparison, and the identity-on-sections coefficient-restriction comparison [def-trf-point-reduction-units]. They satisfy $Q_n\circ P_{n+1}=P_n$. The compatible tuples form $\varprojlim_n H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$. There is an isomorphism $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_nH^0(Y,A_{E,n})$, with $P_n(1_{\mathcal O_E})=1_n$, and $a\mapsto a\cdot1_{\mathcal O_E}$ is bijective.

3. The recorded rational tensor comparison identifies $H^0(Y,E)$ with $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ and sends $1_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes1$ to $1_E$. The map $E\to H^0(Y,E)$, $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot1_E$, is bijective.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, p. 30 (for T discrete and U qcqs, F_T(U)=Map_cont(pi_0(U),T): sections of a constant sheaf on a connected qcqs scheme are constant); literature/milne-lectures-on-etale-cohomology_LEC.pdf, p. 124 (H^r(X,Z_l)=lim H^r(X,Z/l^n), H^r(X,Q_l)=H^r(X,Z_l) (x) Q_l); blueprint prop-cohomological-finiteness, ## Proof, Step 7 ('its space of invariants is all of E, so H^0(Y,E)=E')

proof.text: By [lem-pod-finite-sheaf-h0-augmentation], finite $H^0$ is the sections of $F_n=(A_n)_Y$, with its actual augmentation unit, and negative finite cohomology vanishes. By [lem-pur-proetale-finite-constant-sections] these sections are continuous functions $|Y|\to A_n$, preserving constants and ring operations. Choose $y\in Y$. The fibre of $f(y)$ is nonempty clopen, so connectedness makes it all of $Y$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Evaluation at $y$ is inverse to constants. Thus $u_n$ is $A_n$-linear bijective and $u_n(1)=1_n$. For coefficient reduction both functions agree on every open fibre where a section is constant; hence reduction sends $u_{n+1}(a)$ to $u_n(\bar a)$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, connected case of the discrete continuous-function description

proof.text: Use [lem-pod-constant-direct-image-tower-realization] to identify the integral point complex with the derived limit of the finite point complexes, retaining $P_n,Q_n$ and $Q_nP_{n+1}=P_n$. The negative-degree vanishing of Step 1 gives finite (zero) $H^{-1}$ at every level, so [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler] makes the projection-to-tuples map $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to\varprojlim_nH^0(Y,A_n)$ an isomorphism. No higher-cohomology finiteness is used.

source.place: Tag 0D6K, lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim, applied on the target point site; Milnor at degree zero

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](2) to the module $\mathcal O_E$ generated by $1$. Its completion isomorphism is $a\mapsto(a\bmod\varpi_E^n)_n$. Through Steps 1-2 the tuple of finite units has a unique preimage $1_{\mathcal O_E}$; $a\cdot1_{\mathcal O_E}$ projects to $u_n(a\bmod\varpi_E^n)$. Consequently the scalar-unit map is bijective and every $P_n$ carries the integral unit to $1_n$.

source.place: Tag 00MA, lemma-completion-tensor (3), via the converse finite-module reconstruction statement; Milne pp. 123-124

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-rational-ordinary-cohomology-tensor] to $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ in degree zero. Its canonical isomorphism sends $1_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes1$ to $1_E$. Tensor the scalar-unit isomorphism of Step 3 and its inverse with $E$. Under $\mathcal O_E\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E=E$ their composites remain identities, and the resulting map is $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot1_E$. This proves clause (3).

statement_change.old_statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $Y$ be a nonempty connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] separated finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k$-scheme, and use the cohomology groups $H^0(Y,\Lambda)=H^0(Y,\Lambda_Y)$ of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] for $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E\}$, with $(A_{E,n})_Y$ the constant sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].

1. For every $n\geq1$, $H^0(Y,A_{E,n})=\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},(A_{E,n})_Y)$ (the derived direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image] of a sheaf placed in degree $0$ has the direct image as $\mathcal H^0$), and the map $A_{E,n}\to H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$, $a\mapsto a\cdot1$, where $1$ is the unit section of the sheaf of rings $(A_{E,n})_Y$, is an isomorphism.

2. The maps $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ induced by the projections of the derived limit defining $Ra_{Y*}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ [def-weil-derived-direct-image] (with $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\cong(A_{E,n})_Y$ [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]) induce an isomorphism $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_nH^0(Y,A_{E,n})\cong\varprojlim_nA_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E$; let $1_{\mathcal O_E}\in H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ be the element corresponding to $1$.

3. $H^0(Y,E)=H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ (by the definition of $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ at $E$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and flatness of $E$ over $\mathcal O_E$), and the map $E\to H^0(Y,E)$, $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot1_E$ with $1_E=1_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes1$, is an isomorphism of $E$-vector spaces.
statement_change.what: The previous Lean conclusion quantified arbitrary linear equivalences and only imposed the tautological equation e(a)=a•e(1), so it asserted rank one without identifying H⁰ with pro-etale sections, the projection maps, the inverse-limit compatibility, or the rational tensor unit. The completion conjunct was also a Y-independent restatement of the coefficient tower theorem. The corrected statement names the finite unit classes, coefficient transitions, projection maps and rational tensor normalization required by the source and by downstream unit-section arguments. The finite map is specified through the resolution augmentation rather than a derived-limit projection; the completed comparison explicitly states Q_n composed with P_(n+1)=P_n. The added recorded point-reduction node supplies the identity-on-sections coefficient-restriction square, transported through the actual localization choices.
